name: Yugoslavian Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Pavlič, Matic (2021). Razlikovalne, odvisne in proste fonološke oznake v slovenskem znakovnem jeziku. Slavistična revija 69(1): 83-102.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology article (minimal pairs for handshape, movement, place, non-manuals; phonological processes: assimilation, weakening, deletion, epenthesis). No word on stress/accent (naglas); only says non-manual markers serve 'za označevanje prozodije' (p. 91) and mentions the 'prozodična beseda oziroma kretnja' as the domain of phonological processes (p. 96).

sources.citation: Pavlič, Matic (2022). Selected topics in Slovenian Sign Language linguistics: from minimal pairs to question formation. Hrvatska revija za rehabilitacijska istraživanja 58 (Special Issue): 175-193. doi:10.31299/hrri.58.si.9
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Section 4.1 Phonology (pp. 178-179) covers the four manual parameters and phonemic non-manuals via minimal pairs; nothing on stress, accent or prominence. 'Prosodic pause'/'prosodic marking' mentioned only as clause-level boundary cues (pp. 185-186).

sources.citation: Pavlič, Matic (2023). Including the Sign Language Community in Language Research, Learning and Teaching: Video Reference Grammar of Slovenian Sign Language. Journal of Language and Education 9(4): 60-72. doi:10.17323/jle.2023.11999
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes the SZJ video reference grammar; its phonology chapter units (table p. 68) are place of articulation, handshape, phonological features, movement, non-manual markings - no prosody/stress unit. No stress statement in the article.

sources.citation: Raičević Bajić, Dragana, Myriam Vermeerbergen, Adam Schembri & Mieke Van Herreweghe (2021). Constituent order in Serbian Sign Language declarative clauses. Glossa 6(1): 51. doi:10.5334/gjgl.1357
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Syntax study; prosody used only as a clause-segmentation criterion (pause >= 80 ms, head nod, squint; section 4.2). Nothing on stress or sign-level prominence.

sources.citation: Pavlič, Matic (2016). The word order parameter in Slovenian Sign Language: transitive, ditransitive, classifier and locative constructions. PhD thesis, Università Ca' Foscari Venezia, 250 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress statement. Explicitly says SZJ prosody is undescribed: fn. 56 p. 158 'no research has been carried out on setting prosodic boundaries in SZJ'; p. 177 'SZJ prosody has not been researched at all'. Prosodic breaks (eye-blink, pause) are assumed from cross-linguistic sign-language literature only.

sources.citation: Vintar, Špela (PI) (2015). Zaključno poročilo raziskovalnega projekta J6-4081 'Korpus in pilotna slovnica slovenskega znakovnega jezika' (ARRS-RPROJ-ZP-2015/191).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Project report; states the planned pilot grammar of SZJ was not built (p. 238-246 of text). No linguistic description, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Dimić, Nadežda, Vesna Polovina & Zorka Kašić (2009). O srpskom znakovnom jeziku [The Serbian sign language]. Beogradska defektološka škola 2009(1): 1-28.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Image-only scan, scanned (200 dpi, tesseract srp). 'Фонологија СЗЈ' pp. 6-7 lists five parameters (handshape, movement, orientation, localisation, facial expression) and processes (epenthesis, metathesis, assimilation, neutralisation) and says a detailed phonological analysis is not attempted; no stress/accent statement. p. 10 (Композиција) says only that, by analogy with spoken and other sign languages, the first sign of a compound is expected to become 'краћи и мање наглашен' (shorter and less stressed) - an expectation, not an SZJ finding. 'акценат' otherwise appears only about spoken Serb…
